requirements.requirement: Configure a backend on node1 TCP port 8091 that returns `backend-ready`.
requirements.summary: The backend listened on TCP 8091 and returned exactly `backend-ready` both before and after a node restart; its systemd service was active and enabled after recovery.

requirements.requirement: Publish the backend through a reverse proxy on node1 TCP port 8090.
requirements.summary: A distinct socat listener on TCP 8090 forwarded to TCP 8091, and requests through port 8090 returned exactly `backend-ready` before and after restart.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: it records a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged reboot scheduling, a boot-ID change from 4eaf428d-1724-4431-a764-c9e0fdc350cc to f9af3214-0ab3-498f-9191-b4387db5bbd6, and recovered system, services, listeners, and responses. Fixed lifecycle observations independently corroborate the boot-ID transition and recovered sockets.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The backend files and service created by cmd-824c3590015d493a and the proxy service created by cmd-a6970ec66cc241c1 directly served the task. The reboot scheduled by cmd-9582fa4ab0ca4b6b was required by the provider-wide restart protocol. Connection failures during reboot were expected observations, not mutations. Afterward there were no failed units or package-database errors; the new systemd-private temporary directories were normal runtime artifacts of the required services.
